stem:
Alok searches 12-hour clock times for a digit pattern: all four digits are the same, and the time must be valid on a 12-hour clock.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $11{:}11$ works, because its four digits match and it is a valid 12-hour time.
$13{:}13$ works, because its four digits match, even though $13$ is not a 12-hour hour.
A valid 12-hour time produces the matching-digit pattern, so first pick any valid time and then force its digits to match.
$22{:}22$ on a 24-hour clock counts the same way, so the 12-hour validity check can be skipped.

teacher.key_rationale: 11:11 has four matching digits and is valid on a 12-hour clock. 13:13 omits 12-hour validity; reversing so a time invents the pattern, or scoring 24-hour displays the same way, miss the hinge.
